description.narrative: In the context of today’s challenges strengthening water governance and adopting innovative technologies are critical for addressing India’s water challenges, with international collaboration playing an important role in supporting these efforts. Water management forms a key component of the Netherlands’ international engagement through the Partners for Water (PfW) Programme 2022-2027, implemented by the Netherlands Enterprise and Development Agency (RVO) on behalf of the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management under the Netherlands International Water Ambition (NIWA).As part of this collaboration, a market scan will be undertaken to identify where Dutch knowledge, services, and technologies can support India’s water sector priorities. It will examine opportunities across key thematic areas relevant to both India’s priorities and Dutch expertise, including climate resilience and flood management; river basin management and river rejuvenation; wastewater treatment and reuse; drinking water supply and rural water services; urban water services and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH); water-use efficiency; water infrastructure, such as dams and reservoirs; and groundwater management. These thematic areas will be further explored through analytical domains such as urban water and river management; artificial intelligence (AI) and geospatial applications; modelling and management of river dynamics; monitoring and modelling of water quality; and river economy and finance, reflecting areas where Dutch expertise can contribute to addressing India’s water sector challenges. Cross-cutting aspects such as policy and planning frameworks, climate resilience, and nature-based solutions will be considered across these themes.Geographically, the assignment will cover the water sector landscape at the national scale, with particular engagement around the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) and the Ganga basin, as well as selected states.
